summary.title: Writing a C Compiler, Part 5
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add local variables (declaration, assignment, reference) to a toy C compiler, using stack frames, EBP-relative offsets, and a variable map during code generation.
takeaways: Local variables are stored on the stack and located via offsets from EBP, which stays fixed during a function call while ESP changes.
Assignment is modeled as an expression (right-associative, lowest precedence) rather than a binary operator, so a = b = 2 is valid.
Variable declarations, assignments and references are generated with a variable map from names to stack offsets, which fails on redeclaration or undeclared use.
Function prologue (push ebp; movl esp, ebp) and epilogue (movl ebp, esp; pop ebp; ret) are needed, and main must return 0 when the return statement is missing.
summary.summary: This fifth post in Nora Sandler's C compiler series adds local int variables restricted to main, with declaration, assignment and reference. It extends the lexer with the = token, updates the AST and grammar so functions contain statement lists and assignment is an expression, and explains the parser changes. The code generation section covers stack frames, the prologue and epilogue, tracking variable locations in an immutable map, and why main should return 0 when no return statement is present, citing the C11 standard.
